import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Data preprocessing for visualization
df['age_group'] = pd.cut(df['age'], bins=[0, 12, 18, 35, 60, 80], labels=['Child', 'Teen', 'Young Adult', 'Adult', 'Senior'])
df.dropna(subset=['age_group', 'embarked'], inplace=True)
df['survived_label'] = df['survived'].map({0: 'Did not survive', 1: 'Survived'})

# Set up the plot style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.facecolor": (0, 0, 0, 0)})

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8), dpi=150)

# Create the violin plot combined with a swarm plot
sns.violinplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass',
    y='age',
    hue='survived_label',
    split=True,
    inner='quartile',
    palette={'Survived': 'lightgreen', 'Did not survive': '#ff9999'},
    ax=ax
)

sns.stripplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass',
    y='age',
    hue='survived_label',
    dodge=True,
    jitter=0.2,
    alpha=0.4,
    size=3,
    palette={'Survived': 'darkgreen', 'Did not survive': 'darkred'},
    ax=ax
)

# Improve plot aesthetics and labels
ax.set_title('Survival on the Titanic: Age Distribution by Passenger Class', fontsize=18, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Age', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_xticklabels(['1st Class', '2nd Class', '3rd Class'])
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%d'))

# Customize the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# We only want to show the violin plot legend entries, which are the first two
ax.legend(handles[0:2], labels[0:2], title='Survival Status', loc='upper left')

# Add an insightful annotation
ax.annotate(
    'Children in 2nd and 3rd class\nhad a higher survival rate',
    xy=(1.9, 5),
    xytext=(1.5, 40),
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=8),
    fontsize=10,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="yellow", ec="k", lw=1, alpha=0.8)
)

# Final layout adjustment
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
